Science.name: Photosynthesis
Science.definition: Photosynthesis converts light energy, water, and carbon dioxide into glucose and oxygen inside chloroplasts.
key_facts: During the light-independent reactions of this process, the enzyme RuBisCO fixes carbon dioxide within the stroma of chloroplasts. It relies on chlorophyll pigments to absorb solar energy and uses water to generate glucose and oxygen gas. For the point, name this process by which green plants convert light energy into chemical energy.

Science.name: Velocity
Science.definition: Velocity is a vector quantity that represents the rate and direction of an object's motion.
key_facts: The time derivative of this quantity equals acceleration, while integrating it over time yields an object's overall displacement. Unlike speed, this property accounts for both magnitude and direction, defining it as a vector quantity. For the point, name this physical vector quantity defined as the rate of change of position.

Science.name: Cell Biology
Science.definition: Mitochondria generate cellular energy in the form of ATP via aerobic respiration and are known as cellular powerhouses.
key_facts: This organelle contains inner membrane folds called cristae that increase surface area for ATP synthase during the electron transport chain. It possesses its own independent circular DNA, supporting the endosymbiotic theory of its evolution. For the point, name this double-membraned organelle commonly called the powerhouse of the cell.

Science.name: Plate Tectonics
Science.definition: Convergent boundaries occur where tectonic plates collide, resulting in subduction zones or mountain-building uplift.
key_facts: Subduction zones at these locations form deep oceanic trenches and volcanic arcs, such as those forming the Pacific Ring of Fire. These zones occur when two tectonic plates move toward one another and collide, forming mountains or subducting under each other. For the point, name these tectonic plate boundaries contrasted with divergent and transform boundaries.

Science.name: Thermodynamics
Science.definition: Temperature measures the average translational kinetic energy of molecules within a system.
key_facts: Absolute zero on the Kelvin scale represents the theoretical point at which this property reaches its minimum possible value. According to kinetic theory, it reflects the average kinetic energy of particles within a system. For the point, name this physical property measured using the Celsius, Fahrenheit, or Kelvin scales.

Science.name: Photosynthesis
Science.definition: Photosynthesis consists of light-dependent reactions and the light-independent Calvin cycle catalyzed by RuBisCO in plant chloroplasts.
key_facts: The first step of light-independent reactions in this biological process is catalyzed by the enzyme RuBisCO. It takes place within the stroma of chloroplasts where carbon dioxide is fixed into 3-phosphoglycerate molecules. For the point, name this process used by plants to convert solar energy into chemical energy in the form of glucose.

Science.name: Velocity
Science.definition: Velocity is a vector quantity representing the rate of change of position, incorporating both speed and direction.
key_facts: In specialized applications of fluid dynamics, the terminal value of this vector quantity occurs when drag force equals gravitational force on a falling object. It is mathematically defined as the derivative of position with respect to time. For the point, name this vector physical quantity that measures both the speed and direction of an object's motion.

Science.name: Thermodynamics
Science.definition: Entropy measures the degree of disorder or randomness in a system and increases in spontaneous isolated processes.
key_facts: This thermodynamic quantity measures the amount of thermal energy per unit temperature that is unavailable for doing useful work. According to the Second Law of Thermodynamics, this value in an isolated system always increases over time during spontaneous processes. For the point, name this measure of disorder or randomness in a physical system.

Science.name: Periodic Table & Elements
Science.definition: Tungsten (symbol W, atomic number 74) possesses the highest melting point of all pure metals.
key_facts: Denoted by the symbol W from its alternative name Wolfram, this transition metal has the highest melting point of all discovered pure metals. It is commonly alloyed to form extremely hard cutting tools and was historically used as the filament in incandescent light bulbs. For the point, name this chemical element with atomic number 74.

Science.name: Acceleration
Science.definition: Acceleration measures the rate at which an object's velocity changes over time.
key_facts: Represented by the letter g near Earth's surface, this quantity has an approximate standard value of 9.81 meters per second squared. According to Newton's second law, multiplying mass by this quantity yields net force. For the point, name this rate of change of velocity over time.

Science.name: Photosynthesis
Science.definition: Photosynthesis uses light energy to synthesize organic compounds from carbon dioxide and water inside plant chloroplasts.
key_facts: The light-independent reactions of this process take place within the stroma and utilize ATP and NADPH produced during the light-dependent stage. RuBisCO catalyzes the initial step of carbon fixation during its Calvin cycle. For the point, name this biological process by which green plants convert light energy into chemical energy.

Science.name: Thermodynamics
Science.definition: Entropy is a measure of molecular randomness in a system, quantified by the symbol S.
key_facts: The absolute zero of temperature is defined as the point at which this thermodynamic property reaches a constant minimum value according to Nernst's heat theorem. Stated in the second law of thermodynamics, this state function measures the degree of randomness or disorder in a closed system. For the point, name this physical property denoted by the letter S.

Science.name: Genetics
Science.definition: DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) stores genetic code in a double-stranded helical structure.
key_facts: This molecular structure features antiparallel strands held together by hydrogen bonds between complementary purine and pyrimidine bases. First modeled by James Watson and Francis Crick using X-ray crystallography data collected by Rosalind Franklin, it carries genetic instructions in living organisms. For the point, name this double-helix nucleic acid containing deoxyribose sugar.

Science.name: Velocity
Science.definition: Velocity is a vector quantity expressing speed alongside direction of motion.
key_facts: This vector quantity is defined as the rate of change of displacement with respect to time, unlike its scalar counterpart which represents speed. Graphically, it corresponds to the derivative of position with respect to time. For the point, name this physical quantity that specifies both the speed and direction of an object in motion.

Science.name: Acceleration
Science.definition: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity per unit time, measured in m/s².
key_facts: In uniform circular motion, this vector points directly toward the center of the circular trajectory and is termed centripetal. Defined in Newton's second law as force divided by mass, it measures the rate at which velocity changes over time. For the point, name this quantity usually expressed in meters per second squared.

Geography.name: World Capitals & Urban Centers
Geography.definition: Istanbul spans both Europe and Asia across the Bosporus Strait and was previously known as Byzantium and Constantinople.
key_facts: This city's historic core contains the district of Sultanahmet and the ancient Byzantine Hippodrome. Located on both sides of the Bosporus strait, it was historically known as Byzantium and Constantinople. For the point, name this most populous city in Turkey.

Geography.name: Physical Geography
Geography.definition: The Great Rift Valley is a continuous geological trench formed by tectonic plate divergence through East Africa.
key_facts: This geographical region includes the Danakil Depression, one of the lowest and hottest places on Earth. Formed by the divergence of the African and Arabian tectonic plates, it extends thousands of kilometers from Syria southwards to Mozambique. For the point, name this massive continuous trench running through East Africa.

Geography.name: Rivers & Lakes
Geography.definition: The Caspian Sea is the world's largest inland body of water, bounded by Russia, Iran, and three Central Asian nations.
key_facts: This body of water receives flow from the Volga and Ural rivers but lacks any natural outlets, making it an endorheic basin. Geologically classified as the world's largest lake by surface area, its waters are partially saline. For the point, name this landlocked sea bordered by Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran, and Azerbaijan.

Geography.name: Deserts & Arid Regions
Geography.definition: Antarctica is technically the largest desert in the world due to its extremely low average annual precipitation.
key_facts: The McMurdo Dry Valleys within this landmass are among the driest places on Earth and feature hyper-saline bodies of water such as Don Juan Pond. Although it holds nearly 70 percent of the world's fresh water in its massive ice sheet, its extremely low annual precipitation classifies it as a desert. For the point, name this southernmost continent.

Geography.name: Islands & Archipelagos
Geography.definition: Madagascar is an island nation off the southeastern coast of mainland Africa in the Indian Ocean.
key_facts: This island's interior plateau includes the Ankaratra Range and its capital city of Antananarivo. Separated from the African continent by the Mozambique Channel, it is famous for its isolated evolution and endemic species like lemurs. For the point, name this large island nation located off the southeast coast of Africa.

Geography.name: World Capitals & Urban Centers
Geography.definition: Burundi shifted its official capital from Bujumbura to Gitega in 2018.
key_facts: Located at the confluence of the Kagera and Ruvubu rivers near Lake Victoria, this country's political administration shifted away from Bujumbura in 2018. The country is bordered by Rwanda, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Tanzania. For the point, name this East African landlocked country whose official capital city was moved to Gitega.

Geography.name: Rivers & Hydrography
Geography.definition: The Rio Grande originates in Colorado, flows through New Mexico, and forms the border between Texas and Mexico.
key_facts: Originating in the San Juan Mountains of Colorado, this river flows past Elephant Butte Dam and forms part of the border near El Paso and Ciudad Juárez. It acts as a natural boundary along the entire southern border of Texas. For the point, name this major river that forms a long portion of the international border between the United States and Mexico.

Geography.name: Mountain Ranges & Volcanoes
Geography.definition: The Alborz Mountains span northern Iran and contain Mount Damavand, the highest peak in the Middle East.
key_facts: The highest peak of this volcanic mountain range is Mount Damavand, which sits near the southern coast of the Caspian Sea. Running through northern Iran, it isolates the central Iranian plateau from northern maritime humidity. For the point, name this major mountain range located in northern Iran.

Geography.name: Islands & Archipelagos
Geography.definition: Sumatra is a large island in western Indonesia, famous for Lake Toba and its extensive biodiversity.
key_facts: Separated from the Asian mainland by the Strait of Malacca, this island contains Lake Toba, the largest volcanic lake on Earth. It is the sixth-largest island in the world and home to major cities like Medan and Palembang. For the point, name this large western Indonesian island located west of Java and Borneo.

Geography.name: Deserts & Arid Regions
Geography.definition: The Atacama Desert in Chile is recognized as the driest non-polar desert on Earth.
key_facts: Formed by the rain shadow effect of the Andes mountains, this region features weather stations that have recorded no rainfall for decades. Rich in sodium nitrate and lithium deposits, it is considered the driest non-polar desert in the world. For the point, name this desert located in northern Chile.

Geography.name: World Capitals & Urban Centers
Geography.definition: Bogotá is the high-altitude capital city of Colombia, situated in the Andes mountains.
key_facts: This city's historic district includes the neighborhood of La Candelaria and the mountaintop sanctuary of Monserrate overlooking its vast savanna. Located on a high plateau in the Eastern Cordillera of the Andes, it lies at an elevation of over 2,600 meters above sea level. For the point, name this capital city of Colombia.

Geography.name: Rivers & Lakes
Geography.definition: The Caspian Sea is the world's largest inland body of water, bounded by Europe and Asia.
key_facts: This body of water is fed by the Volga, Ural, and Kura Rivers and has no outlet to the open ocean, making it an endorheic basin. Bordered by five countries including Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, and Azerbaijan, it contains major offshore oil fields such as Kashagan. For the point, name this body of water, the world's largest inland body of water by surface area.

Geography.name: Physical Geography
Geography.definition: The Pacific Ring of Fire is a major area in the basin of the Pacific Ocean where tectonic plates interact, causing frequent earthquakes and volcanic eruptions.
key_facts: Mount Pinatubo's major 1991 eruption on the island of Luzon occurred within this geologically active zone. Containing approximately 75 percent of Earth's active volcanoes, this region is shaped by subduction along oceanic trenches surrounding a ocean basin. For the point, name this horseshoe-shaped region of intense seismic and volcanic activity surrounding the Pacific Ocean.

Geography.name: Islands & Archipelagos
Geography.definition: Tasmania is an Australian island state south of the mainland, famous for the Tasmanian devil and its capital Hobart.
key_facts: This island is separated from the mainland by the Bass Strait and features unique native wildlife including a carnivorous marsupial named for its loud scream. Its capital city of Hobart sits near Mount Wellington and the mouth of the Derwent River. For the point, name this Australian island state located south of Victoria.

Geography.name: Physical Geography
Geography.definition: The Atacama Desert in northern Chile is celebrated as Earth's driest non-polar desert region.
key_facts: This hyper-arid desert hosts the ALMA radio telescope array due to its extremely low humidity and clear skies at high altitude. Situated along the Pacific coast of South America west of the Andes, it lies within a rain shadow that prevents rainfall. For the point, name this desert in northern Chile, considered the driest non-polar desert in the world.
